entries.title: Create Advertising Campaign
entries.summary: Set up a new advertiser campaign with its placement, schedule, pricing, and delivery goals.
entries.content:
About This Page

Set up a new advertiser campaign with its placement, schedule, pricing, and delivery goals.

Before You Begin

Confirm the advertiser, approved commercial terms, placement availability, campaign dates, and required creative format.

Fields and Options

Advertiser

The organization responsible for the campaign.

Name

A descriptive campaign name used in administration and advertiser reporting.

Placement

The advertising inventory location where the campaign will run.

Status

The campaign's current workflow state.

Start and End

The date and time range during which the campaign may deliver.

Billing Model

The commercial model used for the campaign, such as flat, CPM, CPC, or sponsorship.

Budget or Contract Value

The campaign's financial limit or agreed value, entered according to the form's displayed units.

Impression Goal

The target number of ad impressions, when applicable.

Click Goal

The target number of clicks, when applicable.

Frequency or Delivery Limits

Controls that restrict how frequently or broadly the campaign may be displayed.

Notes

Internal setup, approval, scheduling, or customer instructions.

How to Complete This Page

  1. Select the advertiser and enter a descriptive campaign name.
  2. Choose the placement and supported billing model.
  3. Set the campaign schedule and commercial limits.
  4. Enter delivery goals and restrictions when they apply.
  5. Add useful internal notes and save the campaign.
  6. Add and submit the required creative assets before activation.

What Happens Next

The campaign is saved in its workflow state. Delivery depends on the campaign status, schedule, placement, and approved creative assets.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Do not activate a campaign before checking inventory and creative approval.
  • Review time zones when exact start or end times matter.
  • Changing an active campaign may affect reporting and contracted delivery.

entries.title: Add Campaign Creative
entries.summary: Add a new creative asset and destination to an advertising campaign.
entries.content:
About This Page

Add a new creative asset and destination to an advertising campaign.

Before You Begin

Confirm the campaign placement's required format and dimensions, and verify that the destination URL is ready.

Fields and Options

Name or Label

A short description that distinguishes this creative from other campaign variations.

Creative Type or Format

The type of asset being supplied, such as image, video, banner, or native creative.

File or Image

The visual asset uploaded or selected for the creative.

Headline and Copy

The visible advertising message, when supported by the placement.

Destination URL

The page opened when a visitor selects the advertisement.

Alternative Text

A concise accessible description of the image when the form provides this option.

Tracking or Reference Values

Optional identifiers used for campaign measurement or internal organization.

Status

The creative's current draft, submission, or approval state.

How to Complete This Page

  1. Enter a recognizable name for the creative.
  2. Upload or select the correct visual asset.
  3. Complete the headline, copy, alternative text, and destination fields that apply.
  4. Preview the creative and check for cropping, readability, and placement compatibility.
  5. Save the creative, then submit it for approval when it is complete.

What Happens Next

The creative remains associated with the campaign. It must meet the required workflow status before it can be used for normal campaign delivery.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Use a secure and functioning destination URL.
  • Avoid placing essential text too close to image edges.
  • Editing an approved creative may require another review.

About This Page

Use this page to review every creative variation associated with the selected advertising campaign.

Creative Information

Shows whether a creative is a draft, submitted, approved, rejected, or returned for revision.

Format and Dimensions

entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to manage the operational campaigns that deliver advertisements across configured placements.

Page Features

Campaign Status

Shows whether a campaign is in draft, awaiting approval, active, paused, completed, rejected, or another supported state.

Schedule

Defines when the campaign may deliver.

Placement

Identifies the inventory location used by the campaign.

entries.content:
About This Page

This workspace is the central administrative record for an advertising campaign.

Information on This Page

Campaign Summary

Shows the advertiser, placement, schedule, status, billing model, and delivery goals.

Creatives

Lists the files and variations submitted for the campaign and their approval states.

Delivery Metrics

Shows recorded impressions, clicks, pacing, or other available performance information.

Workflow Actions

Allows authorized staff to submit, approve, reject, pause, or otherwise manage the campaign.

Billing Relationship

Connects the campaign to related invoice or sponsorship information when available.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the campaign setup and confirm its current status.
  2. Check that at least one appropriate creative has been added and approved.
  3. Verify dates, placement capacity, and commercial limits.
  4. Use only the workflow action that reflects the actual administrative decision.
  5. Monitor delivery while the campaign is active.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Campaign approval and creative approval are related but separate controls.
  • Rejected items should include enough information for correction.
  • Preserve campaign history rather than rewriting completed work.

entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to understand which advertising placements are available, nearing capacity, or fully allocated.

Inventory Information

Placement

The site location and format where advertising may appear.

Capacity

The maximum number of campaigns that may be active in the placement.

Active Load

The number of campaigns currently using the placement.

Availability

The remaining capacity available for new campaigns.

Pricing

The placement's configured base price and billing model.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review placements with limited or no remaining capacity.
  2. Compare requested campaign dates against existing allocations.
  3. Open the related placement or campaign when adjustments are required.
  4. Use the inventory information before finalizing sponsorship proposals or campaign dates.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Availability can change as campaigns are approved, paused, completed, or rescheduled.
  • Capacity is not a substitute for checking creative format and campaign date compatibility.
  • Inactive placements should not be promised in new proposals.

entries.content:
About This Page

Define a new advertising location, creative format, capacity, and price.

Fields and Options

Name

The readable name used by administrators and advertisers.

Code

The unique system identifier for the placement.

Location

A description of where the advertisement appears in the site or application.

Format

The supported creative format, such as banner, card, hero, native, or video.

Width and Height

The expected creative dimensions.

Maximum Active Campaigns

The largest number of campaigns that may use the placement at the same time.

Base Price Cents

The reference price entered in cents.

Pricing Model

The billing approach used for the placement, such as flat, CPM, CPC, or sponsorship.

Active

Controls whether the placement may be selected for new work.

Description

Additional guidance about the placement, audience, restrictions, or intended use.

How to Complete This Page

  1. Enter a clear name, unique code, and location description.
  2. Select the creative format and enter the expected dimensions.
  3. Set the maximum active campaign capacity.
  4. Enter the base price in cents and select the pricing model.
  5. Set the active status and add any useful description.
  6. Select Save Placement.

What Happens Next

The placement becomes available to sponsorship packages, proposals, campaigns, creatives, and inventory reporting according to its status.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Coordinate code and dimension changes with the site implementation.
  • Do not activate a placement until the display location is ready.
  • Review existing campaigns before reducing capacity.

About This Page

Ad placements define where advertising can appear and the operating rules for each location.

Page Features

Placement Code

A unique identifier used by campaign and display logic.

Location and Format

Describe where the placement appears and the type of creative it supports.

Dimensions

The expected width and height for compatible creative files.

Capacity

Limits how many campaigns may be active in the placement.

Pricing Model

Defines whether the placement uses flat, CPM, CPC, sponsorship, or another supported pricing method.

Active Status

Controls whether the placement may be used for new advertising work.

How to Use This Page

entries.title: Create Advertising Invoice
entries.summary: Build a draft advertiser invoice from campaign or sponsorship line items.
entries.content:
About This Page

Build a draft advertiser invoice from campaign or sponsorship line items.

Before You Begin

Verify the advertiser's billing information and confirm the authorized charges before preparing the invoice.

Fields and Options

Advertiser

The organization responsible for paying the invoice.

Campaign

The advertising campaign related to the invoice, when applicable.

Due Date

The date by which payment is expected.

Currency

The three-letter currency code, normally USD unless another supported currency is required.

Invoice Items

The products, services, placements, or campaign charges included on the invoice.

Description

A clear explanation of each billed item.

Billing Model

The pricing method used for the item, such as flat, CPM, CPC, or sponsorship.

Quantity

The number of billable units.

Unit Amount Cents

The amount for each unit entered in cents.

Discount Cents

The invoice-level discount entered in cents.

Tax Cents

The invoice-level tax entered in cents.

Estimated Total

The calculated invoice total based on the current items, discount, and tax.

How to Complete This Page

  1. Select the advertiser and related campaign when applicable.
  2. Set the due date and verify the currency.
  3. Add a clear line item for each billable product or service.
  4. Choose the billing model and enter quantity and unit amount in cents.
  5. Enter any authorized discount and applicable tax.
  6. Review the estimated total and select Save Invoice.

What Happens Next

The invoice is saved as a billing record. A draft normally requires a separate issue action before it becomes payable.

Tips and Important Notes

  • All monetary fields on this form use cents.
  • Do not combine unrelated advertisers or legal customers on one invoice.
  • Review invoice edit restrictions after it has been issued or paid.

Invoice Status

Shows whether an invoice is draft, issued, paid, partially paid, void, refunded, overdue, or another supported state.

Advertiser

Amount and Balance

About This Page

This page is the complete billing record for an advertiser invoice.

Information on This Page

Invoice Summary

Shows the advertiser, campaign, issue date, due date, currency, status, total, and remaining balance.

Line Items

Lists the charges, quantities, billing models, and unit amounts.

Payments

Shows payments recorded against the invoice.

Refunds

Shows amounts returned or credited through the supported refund workflow.

Billing Actions

Authorized administrators may issue, void, record payment, record refund, or start checkout when those actions are valid.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the customer, line items, totals, and due date.
  2. Issue the invoice only after confirming its accuracy.
  3. Record payments only after verifying receipt through the appropriate payment source.
  4. Use refunds or void actions only when the financial event actually occurred.
  5. Review the remaining balance after each transaction.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Financial actions may be permanent or restricted after processing.
  • Never record a payment merely to make an invoice appear settled.
  • Keep transaction references and notes sufficient for reconciliation.

About This Page

This audit page records AI Content Studio generation activity for troubleshooting, review, and accountability.

Information on This Page

Feature

The AI-assisted feature that created the record.

Provider and Model

The AI service and model used for the generation.

Status

Shows whether the request completed successfully or encountered an error.

Input

The text or structured request sent for generation.

Output

The generated result returned by the AI service.

Error Message

Technical or policy information recorded when generation failed.

Created Date

The time the generation record was created.

How to Use This Page

  1. Locate the generation by date, feature, status, provider, or model.
  2. Compare the recorded input with the returned output.
  3. Review error information when a generation failed.
  4. Use the record to refine prompts, diagnose provider issues, or verify how content was produced.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Generation history is an audit record, not a final-content approval queue.
  • AI outputs may contain errors even when the status is successful.
  • Avoid sharing logged prompts or outputs outside authorized administrative use.

entries.title: AI Image Prompt Generator
entries.summary: Build structured image-generation prompts using scene details, composition controls, and reusable examples.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use the AI Image Prompt Generator to turn a plain-language scene idea into a detailed prompt for supported image-generation workflows.

Fields and Options

Scene Description

The central subject, activity, environment, and outcome you want the generated prompt to describe.

People and Subject Details

Controls for the number or type of people, appearance, age range, activity, wardrobe state, and other supported subject attributes.

Composition

Options for camera position, framing, orientation, focal emphasis, and arrangement.

Lighting and Style

Controls for lighting, visual mood, realism, rendering style, and overall presentation.

Additional Instructions

Optional requirements, exclusions, or details not covered by the standard controls.

Generated Prompt

The completed prompt returned by the AI service for review and copying.

Recent Generations

A list of recent prompt-generation activity for quick reference.

How to Use This Page

  1. Describe the intended scene in clear, concrete language.
  2. Set the available subject, composition, lighting, style, and output options.
  3. Add any important restrictions or required details.
  4. Generate the prompt.
  5. Review the result carefully and revise the inputs when important details are missing or inaccurate.
  6. Copy the approved prompt into the intended image-generation workflow.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Describe only adults when nudity is involved.
  • Use concrete visual details instead of vague quality terms.
  • AI output may require editing and should not be treated as automatically approved content.
  • Do not enter private customer information or confidential business data.

entries.title: AI Prompt Library
entries.summary: Manage curated example prompts used as structural inspiration by AI Content Studio.
entries.content:
About This Page

The prompt library stores approved examples that help AI Content Studio produce more consistent prompt structures and language.

Page Features

Import JSON

Adds prompt examples from a supported JSON file.

Search

Finds examples by title or prompt content.

Category

Groups examples by subject, purpose, or another organizational label.

Enabled

Controls whether an example may be used by AI-assisted generation.

Disable or Enable

Temporarily removes or restores an example without deleting it.

Delete

Permanently removes an example from the library.

How to Use This Page

  1. Search the library before adding or importing examples.
  2. Review each example for quality, duplication, adult-only requirements, and consistency with Unclad Collection standards.
  3. Disable examples that should be retained for reference but not used for generation.
  4. Import only JSON files prepared for this library's expected format.
  5. Delete an example only when it should no longer be retained.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Examples should provide structural inspiration rather than force every generated prompt to look identical.
  • Remove duplicates and near-duplicates.
  • Do not include minors in prompts involving nudity.
  • Avoid examples containing explicit sexual activity or prohibited content.

entries.title: AI Keyword Exclusions
entries.summary: Manage words and phrases that AI-assisted content should avoid or remove.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to maintain the exclusion vocabulary applied to supported AI content-generation workflows.

Page Features

Add One Exclusion

Adds a single word or phrase with an optional explanation.

Keyword or Phrase

The exact term that should be excluded or treated as undesirable.

Notes

Explains why the term is excluded or how the rule should be interpreted.

Bulk Add

Adds multiple entries separated by commas or new lines.

Search

Filters the current exclusion list.

Edit

Updates an existing exclusion or its notes.

Delete

Removes an exclusion after confirmation.

How to Use This Page

  1. Search the list to make sure the term is not already present.
  2. Use Add One Exclusion when the term needs an explanatory note.

Fields and Options

Title

Name of the person or organization that created the content.
Description
Detailed public-facing description.
Keywords
Search and classification terms associated with the asset.
Asset Files
Upload the files included with the asset and identify the primary preview or poster when applicable.
Asset Type
Choose the type of product or media.
Status
Choose the current publishing or workflow status.
Collection
Optionally associate the asset with a collection.
Sort Order
Controls relative manual ordering where supported.
Active
Allows the record to be used by the application.
Featured
Makes the asset eligible for featured placement.
AI Generated
Identifies content created with generative AI.
Allow quantity selection
Use only when customers may purchase more than one unit.
Fulfillment
Select how the product is delivered.
Collect shipping address
Requests delivery-address fields from the customer.
Shipping address is mandatory
Prevents cart addition until the required address is complete.

  3. Set the primary preview and poster when applicable.

  7. Select Create Asset.

Review canonical terms, variants, synonyms, search volume, result counts, and zero-result activity.

  2. Review its variants and current canonical mapping.

Published entries

Heading shown for this help entry.

entries.title: Edit Page Help
entries.summary: Update an existing Page Help entry, its audience, publication settings, and access restrictions.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to revise help content already associated with an application page.

Before You Begin

Open the target page in another tab when possible so you can verify field labels, buttons, workflows, and the page key while editing its instructions.

Fields and Options

Page Key

Identifies the application page where this help entry appears. Use a key from the Page Help registry or coverage report.

Title

The heading displayed for this help entry in the Help panel.

Summary

A short explanation displayed before the detailed instructions.

Content

The formatted HTML-fragment content containing page instructions, field descriptions, steps, and notes.

Audience

Limits the entry to the selected general audience, such as public, member, advertiser, or administrator.

Roles

Optionally restricts the entry to users who have one of the selected roles.

Permissions

Optionally restricts the entry to users who have one of the selected permissions.

Active

Controls whether the entry is available for use.

Published

Controls whether eligible users can currently see the entry.

Published At

Optionally records or schedules the publication date supported by the form.

Sort Order

Controls the position when several help entries appear on the same page. Lower values appear first.

How to Update the Entry

  1. Confirm that the Page Key still matches the intended application page.
  2. Update the title and summary in plain language.
  3. Revise the detailed content using the established Page Help section structure.
  4. Review audience, role, and permission restrictions.
  5. Confirm active, published, publication date, and sort-order settings.
  6. Select Save Changes.
  7. Open the target page and review the result in the Help panel.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Use exact field and button labels from the application.
  • Do not include complete HTML documents, scripts, or page-level styling.
  • When several entries use the same page key, give each one a distinct purpose and sort order.
  • Export the Page Help seed after approved database changes so they are preserved for future deployments.

entries.title: Managing Page Help

An optional telephone number for the prospect.

How the lead was acquired, such as referral, website inquiry, outreach, or event.

The current position in the sales pipeline.

A percentage from 0 to 100 representing the estimated chance of winning the opportunity.

The lead appears in the sponsorship pipeline and can later be used to prepare a proposal.

  • Update the stage after every meaningful change in the opportunity.
  • Probabilities should reflect evidence, not optimism.

Fields and Options

Name

The customer-facing or internal name used to identify the sponsorship package.

Code

A unique short identifier used to distinguish the package from other offerings.

Duration Days

The standard number of days covered by the package.

Package Price Cents

The package selling price entered in cents. For example, enter 250000 for $2,500.00.

Base Price Cents

The underlying reference value entered in cents, which may be used for comparison or pricing analysis.

Included Creatives

The number of creative files or variations included with the package.

Description

A plain-language explanation of what the package includes and who it is intended for.

Included Placements

The advertising locations that are part of this package.

Active

Controls whether the package is available for new sponsorship work.

How to Complete This Page

  1. Enter a clear package name and unique code.
  2. Set the duration and enter all monetary values in cents.
  3. Describe the package and select every included placement.
  4. Set the active status.
  5. Select Save Package to store the package.

What Happens Next

The saved package becomes available when administrators prepare sponsorship proposals. Existing proposals retain their own saved terms.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Do not reuse an old package code for a materially different offering.
  • Review included placements whenever inventory changes.
  • Deactivate retired packages instead of deleting historical business context.

An optional reusable package used as the starting point for the offer.

The individual placements, services, quantities, and unit prices included in the offer.

Placement

The advertising inventory associated with a proposal item, when applicable.

Quantity

The number of units included for the item.

The amount per unit entered in cents.

Discount Cents

Any discount applied to the proposal, entered in cents.

Tax Cents

Any applicable tax entered in cents.

Terms

Commercial conditions, payment expectations, delivery requirements, and other agreement language.

Notes

Internal notes that help administrators manage the proposal.

How to Complete This Page

  1. Enter a descriptive proposal title and select the advertiser.
  2. Link the lead or package when applicable.
  3. Set the proposed start, end, and expiration dates.
  4. Review each proposal item, placement, quantity, and unit amount.
  5. Enter discounts, taxes, terms, and internal notes as needed.
  6. Select Save Proposal.

What Happens Next

The proposal is saved for review and status management. Saving does not by itself activate advertising inventory or record payment.

Tips and Important Notes

  • All monetary values are entered in cents.
  • Make sure the expiration date allows enough time for review.
  • Do not change accepted commercial terms without creating a documented revision or new proposal.

User administration and impersonation are restricted to authorized administrators.

entries.title: User Details
entries.summary: Review a user’s profile, access, and marketplace activity.
entries.content:
About This Page

This page provides a consolidated view of the selected user, including identity information, access assignments, account status, and related marketplace records.

Reviewing the Account

Profile
Confirm the user’s name, username, email address, and account details.
Roles and permissions
Review the access currently granted to the user.
Customer activity
Use available links to review orders, licenses, downloads, tickets, or other related records.

How to Use This Page

  1. Verify that you are viewing the correct account.
  2. Review account status and assigned roles before making changes.
  3. Use Edit when profile or access information must be updated.
  4. Use related-record links to investigate customer questions or support issues.

Important Notes

  • Customer passwords are never displayed.
  • Use impersonation only for legitimate support or testing purposes.

entries.title: Managing the Advertiser Account
entries.summary: Maintain organization contact and billing details and review portal members.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Account page stores the organization details used for advertiser communication and billing. Only an advertiser owner can edit these details.

Fields and Options

Contact name
Primary person Unclad Collection should contact.
Contact email
Primary operational email address.
Contact phone
Primary telephone number.
Billing email
Address that should receive billing communication.
Website URL
Public website for the advertiser organization.
Billing address
Organization billing address.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the existing contact and billing information.
  2. Owners can update fields that have changed.
  3. Select Save account.
  4. Review Portal members and their assigned roles.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Non-owner members can review the page but cannot edit account details.

entries.title: Creating a Campaign Creative
entries.summary: Upload advertising media and provide its message and destination.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this form to create a new advertisement for the selected campaign.

Fields and Options

Creative name
Enter an internal name that helps identify the advertisement.
Creative media
Upload or select the supported visual used by the placement.
Headline and message
Enter the text displayed with the advertisement where supported.
Destination URL
Enter the complete page visitors should reach after selecting the ad.
Alternative text
Describe the visual for accessibility when the field is available.

How to Use This Page

  1. Enter a clear creative name.
  2. Add the required media.
  3. Complete the message and destination information.
  4. Save the creative as a draft.
  5. Return to the creative list and submit it when it is ready for review.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Confirm that the destination URL works and matches the advertisement.

entries.title: Editing a Campaign Creative
entries.summary: Revise an eligible creative before resubmitting it for review.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this form to correct or improve a draft or rejected campaign creative.

Fields and Options

Creative media
Replace the visual only when a different file is needed.
Message and destination
Update the visible text and landing-page URL.
Review feedback
Use any rejection or revision notes to guide the changes.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the current content and any feedback.
  2. Update the media, message, or destination.
  3. Save the creative.
  4. Submit it again when all requested changes are complete.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Changing a creative may require a new approval before it can run.

entries.title: Managing Campaign Creatives
entries.summary: Review, edit, and submit advertisements for approval.
entries.content:
About This Page

Campaign Creatives contains the images, copy, destinations, and approval state for ads in a campaign.

Page Features

Creative status
Shows whether a creative is draft, submitted, approved, or rejected.
Create creative
Starts a new advertisement for the campaign.
Edit
Updates a draft or rejected creative.
Submit
Sends an eligible creative to the review workflow.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the current creative list and statuses.
  2. Create a new creative or edit an eligible one.
  3. Confirm the media, message, and destination.
  4. Submit the creative for review.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Submitted or approved creatives may be locked from editing until their status changes.

entries.title: Editing an Advertising Campaign
entries.summary: Update advertiser-managed campaign information when editing is permitted.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to revise the editable details of an advertising campaign. Available fields and actions may depend on campaign status and your advertiser membership role.

Page Features

Campaign information
Review the campaign name, schedule, goals, and related details.
Creative and placement information
Confirm the materials and placements associated with the campaign.
Status restrictions
Some fields may become read-only after review, approval, scheduling, or launch.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the existing campaign before making changes.
  2. Update only the fields that need correction.
  3. Confirm dates, budget information, and associated creative details.
  4. Save the campaign.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Contact support or your Unclad Collection representative when a locked campaign requires a change.

entries.title: Managing Advertising Campaigns
entries.summary: Review campaign status, dates, budgets, and performance.
entries.content:
About This Page

My Campaigns lists advertising campaigns available to your advertiser organization.

Page Features

Campaign list
Review each campaign and its current status.
Campaign details
Open a campaign to view dates, placements, creatives, budget, and performance information.
Editing
Use the available edit action when your membership role permits changes.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the campaign list and identify the campaign you need.
  2. Open the campaign for complete details.
  3. Use edit actions only when campaign information needs to be updated.

entries.title: Reviewing a Campaign
entries.summary: View campaign status, dates, placements, budget, and creative activity.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Campaign Details page summarizes the advertising work approved or scheduled for your organization.

Page Features

Campaign summary
Shows the campaign name, status, schedule, and financial information.
Placements
Lists where advertising is scheduled to appear.
Creatives
Provides access to the media and messages assigned to the campaign.
Performance
Shows available delivery or engagement information.

How to Use This Page

  1. Confirm the campaign schedule and current status.
  2. Review the assigned placements.
  3. Open the creative area to upload or manage campaign materials.
  4. Review performance information as delivery begins.

entries.title: Using the Advertiser Portal
entries.summary: Review recent campaigns, invoices, account activity, and advertiser tools.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Advertiser Portal dashboard summarizes the advertiser organization and provides quick access to its active work.

Page Features

Recent campaigns
Review current and recently updated advertising campaigns.
Recent invoices
Open recent billing records and payment information.
Portal navigation
Move to campaigns, creatives, reports, proposals, invoices, or account settings.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review current campaign and billing activity.
  2. Open a recent item that needs attention.
  3. Use the portal navigation for detailed management and reporting.

entries.title: Reviewing Advertising Invoices
entries.summary: Track invoice amounts, balances, due dates, and payment status.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Invoices page lists billing records associated with advertising services.

Page Features

Invoice number
Identifies the billing record.
Status
Shows whether the invoice is open, paid, overdue, void, or refunded.
Balance
Shows the amount still due.
Invoice details
Opens line items, payment history, and payment options.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review invoices with an outstanding balance.
  2. Open an invoice to confirm its line items.
  3. Pay an eligible balance from the invoice details page.

entries.title: Understanding and Paying an Invoice
entries.summary: Review charges, payment history, and pay an outstanding balance.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Invoice Details page provides the complete billing record for advertising services.

Page Features

Line items
Lists the services, quantities, rates, and amounts charged.
Payment history
Shows completed or attempted payments associated with the invoice.
Balance due
Shows the remaining unpaid amount.
Pay action
Starts secure checkout when the invoice is eligible for payment.

How to Use This Page

  1. Confirm the invoice number and organization.
  2. Review every line item and the total.
  3. Review previous payment activity.
  4. Select Pay when a balance is due and the invoice is eligible.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Contact support before paying when the organization, service, or amount appears incorrect.

entries.title: Reviewing Advertising Proposals
entries.summary: View proposals, statuses, totals, and next actions.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Proposals page lists advertising offers prepared for your organization.

Page Features

Proposal status
Shows whether a proposal is pending, accepted, declined, or no longer active.
Proposal total
Shows the proposed financial value.
Details
Opens included services, terms, and acceptance controls.

How to Use This Page

  1. Open a proposal that requires review.
  2. Read all included services and terms.
  3. Accept or decline from the proposal details page.

entries.title: Responding to a Proposal
entries.summary: Review services and terms, then accept or decline the proposal.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Proposal Details page contains the complete offer and records your organization’s response.

Fields and Options

Signer name
Enter the person authorized to accept the proposal.
Title
Enter the signer’s role or position.
Email
Enter the signer’s business email address.
Company
Confirm the organization accepting the proposal.
Decline reason
When declining, explain why the proposal is not a fit.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the proposal details, included services, pricing, and terms.
  2. To accept, complete the signer information and select Accept Proposal.
  3. To decline, enter a clear reason and select Decline Proposal.

What Happens Next

The proposal status is updated and becomes part of the advertising account record.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Only an authorized representative should accept a proposal.

entries.title: Reviewing Advertising Reports
entries.summary: Analyze campaign delivery and engagement results.
entries.content:
About This Page

Advertising Reports summarizes available campaign performance for your organization.

Page Features

Date range
Limits results to the selected reporting period.
Campaign filter
Focuses the report on a specific campaign when available.
Delivery metrics
Shows measures such as impressions, clicks, and other supported outcomes.
Performance breakdown
Compares results across campaigns, creatives, or placements.

How to Use This Page

  1. Choose the reporting period.
  2. Apply a campaign filter when needed.
  3. Review the summary metrics.
  4. Compare creatives or placements to identify stronger performance.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Recently delivered activity may take time to appear in reports.

entries.title: Favorites
entries.summary: Open the default wish list used to save marketplace content for later review.
entries.content:
About This Page

Favorites is the default wish list for quickly saving assets while browsing the marketplace.

How Favorites Work

Saved Assets

Displays the marketplace items currently stored in your default Favorites list.

Remove

Removes an item from Favorites without affecting purchases or other wish lists.

Move

Moves an item to another wish list when that action is available.

Open Asset

Returns to the asset detail page for additional review or purchase.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the assets you saved while browsing.
  2. Open an asset to check current pricing and license options.
  3. Move items into named wish lists when you want to organize a project or collection.
  4. Remove items you no longer need.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Saving an asset does not reserve its price or availability.
  • Removing an asset from Favorites does not remove it from a different wish list.
  • Purchased content remains available through your account library rather than Favorites.

entries.title: Using Your Asset Library
entries.summary: Find purchased assets, licenses, files, and available downloads.
entries.content:
About This Page

Your Asset Library brings together the media you have purchased and the licenses that authorize its use.

Page Features

Search and filters
Find purchases by asset title, order number, license key, or other available filters.
License records
Open the license associated with each purchased asset.
Downloads
Access individual files or a complete download package when the license permits it.

How to Use This Page

  1. Search or browse for the asset you need.
  2. Open the related license to review usage rights and file availability.
  3. Download the required file or complete package.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Download limits and availability depend on the license status and purchased offering.

entries.title: Reviewing a License
entries.summary: Understand licensed use, covered assets, documents, and downloadable files.
entries.content:
About This Page

A license record explains what you purchased and how the associated asset may be used.

Page Features

License details
Shows the license type, key, status, purchase date, and covered use.
Included files
Lists files available under the purchased offering.
License certificate
Provides a downloadable document describing the license.
Proof of purchase
Provides a purchase record for your files.
Download all
Creates or downloads the complete eligible file package.

How to Use This Page

  1. Confirm the asset and license type.
  2. Read the permitted use and any restrictions.
  3. Download the certificate or proof of purchase for your records.
  4. Download individual files or the complete package as needed.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Keep the license key and documents with your project records.
  • A license applies only to the asset, offering, and purchaser shown in the record.

entries.title: Choosing Notification Preferences
entries.summary: Select which optional account and marketing communications you receive.
entries.content:
About This Page

Notification Preferences lets you control optional communications while preserving required service messages.

Page Features

Required service communications
Explains messages that cannot be disabled because they are necessary for purchases, security, licensing, or support.
Communication categories
Groups optional email and in-application notifications by purpose.
Channel controls
Lets you enable or disable supported delivery methods for each category.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the required communications section.
  2. Review each optional category.
  3. Enable only the channels you want to receive.
  4. Save your preferences.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Disabling a marketing category does not stop necessary transactional or security messages.

entries.title: Managing Notifications
entries.summary: Review account alerts and mark them as read.
entries.content:
About This Page

Notifications provide updates about purchases, licenses, wish lists, support, and other account activity.

Page Features

Unread notifications
Highlights updates that have not yet been reviewed.
Mark as read
Updates an individual notification after you review it.
Mark all as read
Clears the unread state from all current notifications.
Notification link
Opens the related order, license, ticket, list, or account page when available.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review unread items first.
  2. Open a notification when it links to a related record.
  3. Mark items as read individually or use Mark all as read.

entries.title: Reviewing Your Orders
entries.summary: View order numbers, dates, totals, payment status, and fulfillment details.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Orders page lists purchases associated with your account and provides access to each order record.

Page Features

Order number
Identifies the purchase for support and recordkeeping.
Status
Shows the current payment or fulfillment state.
Order total
Displays the total charged for the order.
Order details
Opens purchased items, timeline, payment summary, and tracking information.

How to Use This Page

  1. Locate an order by date, number, or status.
  2. Open the order to review its purchased items and history.
  3. Use the order number when contacting support about the purchase.

entries.title: Understanding an Order
entries.summary: Review purchased items, totals, timeline, and shipment tracking.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Order Details page provides the complete record of a purchase.

Page Features

Purchased items
Lists each asset, package, license, quantity, and price included in the order.
Order timeline
Shows important events in the life of the order.
Summary
Displays subtotal, adjustments, taxes, and total.
Tracking
Shows shipment information when an order includes physical fulfillment.

How to Use This Page

  1. Confirm the order number and status.
  2. Review each purchased item and its associated license.
  3. Check the timeline for payment or fulfillment updates.
  4. Review tracking information when it is available.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Use the license area rather than the order page to download licensed digital files.

entries.title: Managing Privacy Preferences
entries.summary: Control personalization, wish-list sharing defaults, and account-data options.
entries.content:
About This Page

Privacy Preferences controls how selected account information and activity are used within Unclad Collection.

Page Features

Personalization
Controls whether account activity may be used to improve recommendations and discovery.
Wish-list sharing
Controls the default privacy behavior available for saved lists.
Account data
Provides information or actions related to your stored account data.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review each privacy section.
  2. Enable or disable the options according to your preference.
  3. Save the changes.

What Happens Next

Your updated choices are applied to future account activity and supported personalization features.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Changing personalization settings may affect the relevance of recommendations.

entries.title: Managing Wish Lists
entries.summary: Create lists and organize assets you may want to revisit or purchase.
entries.content:
About This Page

Wish Lists help you save and group marketplace assets for projects, ideas, or future purchases.

Fields and Options

List name
Enter a clear name that describes the project or purpose.
Description
Optionally explain what belongs in the list.
Visibility
Choose whether the list is private or may be shared, when that option is available.

How to Use This Page

  1. Enter a name for the new list.
  2. Add an optional description.
  3. Create the list.
  4. Open any list to manage its assets, sharing, and notification settings.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Use separate lists for different projects to make saved assets easier to find.

entries.title: Using a Wish List
entries.summary: Review saved assets, manage sharing, and move or remove items.
entries.content:
About This Page

A Wish List contains assets saved for a particular project or purpose.

Page Features

Saved assets
Open an asset, remove it, or move it to another list.
Sharing
Create or disable a share link when the list supports sharing.
Wish-list notifications
Choose whether supported changes to saved assets should create notifications.
List settings
Rename the list or update its description and visibility.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the assets currently saved in the list.
  2. Open an asset to review current availability and licensing.
  3. Move or remove items as needed.
  4. Configure sharing or notifications when useful.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Anyone with an active unlisted share link may be able to view the list. Disable sharing when the link is no longer needed.

entries.title: Choosing Your Appearance
entries.summary: Select the visual theme used while you are signed in.
entries.content:
About This Page

Appearance Settings controls the supported light, dark, or system-based display preference.

Page Features

Light
Uses the light interface theme.
Dark
Uses the dark interface theme.
System
Follows the appearance preference configured on your device or browser.

How to Use This Page

  1. Select the appearance option you prefer.
  2. Confirm that the interface changes as expected.

Tips and Important Notes

  • The System option may change automatically when your device changes between light and dark mode.

entries.title: Reviewing Your Cart
entries.summary: Confirm assets, offerings, licenses, quantities, and totals before checkout.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Cart contains the items selected for purchase and allows you to review the complete order before payment.

Page Features

Cart item
Shows the selected asset, package, license, quantity, and price.
Quantity controls
Increase or decrease quantity when the offering supports multiple units.
Remove
Deletes an individual item from the cart.
Order summary
Shows the current subtotal and other calculated amounts.
Checkout
Begins secure payment for the current cart.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review every asset and selected license.
  2. Adjust quantities where applicable.
  3. Remove any item you do not intend to purchase.
  4. Confirm the order summary.
  5. Select Checkout.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Licenses and digital files may have different terms even when they cover the same asset. Confirm each selection before paying.

entries.title: Checkout Canceled
entries.summary: Return to your cart after leaving or canceling payment.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Checkout Canceled page appears when payment was not completed.

Page Features

Return to cart
Lets you review the selected items and try again.
Continue browsing
Lets you leave checkout without completing the purchase.

How to Use This Page

  1. Return to the cart if you still want the selected items.
  2. Review the cart and payment information.
  3. Begin checkout again when ready.

Tips and Important Notes

  • A canceled checkout does not create a completed purchase.

entries.title: Checkout Completed
entries.summary: Confirm that payment was accepted and open your new purchases.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Checkout Success page confirms that the payment process completed successfully.

Page Features

Confirmation
Shows the successful checkout status and available order information.
Library or order link
Provides access to the purchased assets or order record.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the confirmation information.
  2. Open the order or asset library to verify the purchase.
  3. Download licensed files from the related license record when they become available.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Keep the order number for your records and for any support request.

entries.title: Using the Member Dashboard
entries.summary: Access account tools, purchases, support, and other member features.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Member Dashboard is the signed-in starting point for account-related tools and activity.

Page Features

Account tools
Open your profile, security, preferences, and other account settings.
Purchases and library
Access purchased assets, licenses, and downloads.
Support
Create and review support tickets.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the available account sections.
  2. Open the area related to the task you need to complete.
  3. Return to the dashboard whenever you need to move to another member area.

entries.title: Updating Your Profile
entries.summary: Manage your name, username, profile image, email, and author information.
entries.content:
About This Page

Profile Settings controls the personal and public-facing information associated with your account.

Fields and Options

Name
Enter your full name.
Username
Choose the public username used where supported.
Profile Icon
Upload or choose the image used to represent your account.
Email address
Enter the address used for account communications and verification.
Author Title
For contributors, enter a short professional title.
Author Bio
For contributors, provide a concise biography.
Author Website URL
For contributors, enter a complete website address beginning with https://.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review your current account information.
  2. Update the fields that need to change.
  3. Save the profile.
  4. Complete email verification when changing to a new email address requires it.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Use author fields only when your profile appears on published stories or contributor content.

entries.title: Using My Library
entries.summary: Search purchased assets, review license details, and access available downloads.
entries.content:
About This Page

My Library contains the assets and licenses associated with your purchases.

Page Features

Search
Search by asset title, order number, or license key.
Library records
Review the purchased asset, associated license, order information, and download availability.
License details
Open a record for complete license and purchase information.

How to Use This Page

  1. Enter a search value when you need a specific purchase.
  2. Select Search to apply it.
  3. Open the matching asset or license record.
  4. Use the available download action for eligible files.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Download availability and limits depend on the license and account status.

entries.title: Purchase Details
entries.summary: Review a purchased image, related order information, license access, and available downloads.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to review the details and fulfillment options associated with a previously purchased image.

Purchase Information

Purchased Image

Identifies the content included in the purchase.

Order

Shows the transaction associated with the purchase.

License

Identifies the license terms that apply to your use of the image.

Downloads

Provides access to available licensed files while the license and download entitlement remain valid.

Documents

May provide a license certificate, proof of purchase, or related records.

How to Use This Page

  1. Confirm that you are viewing the correct image and order.
  2. Review the license before using the downloaded content.
  3. Download the file format appropriate for your project.
  4. Save the license documents with your project records.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Do not share download links or licensed source files outside the rights granted by the license.
  • Download availability may be affected by license status or account restrictions.
  • Contact Support when a purchased file is missing, damaged, or unavailable.

entries.title: Updating Account Security
entries.summary: Change your password and review security-related account controls.
entries.content:
About This Page

Security Settings protects access to your account and allows you to replace your current password.

Fields and Options

Current password
Enter the password currently protecting the account.
New password
Enter a strong password that meets the displayed requirements.
Confirm password
Enter the new password again exactly.

How to Use This Page

  1. Enter your current password.
  2. Enter and confirm the new password.
  3. Save the password change.

What Happens Next

The new password becomes effective after the update succeeds.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Use a unique password that you do not use on other websites.
  • Never share your password with support staff.

entries.title: Creating a Support Ticket
entries.summary: Create an account-linked support request with a category, subject, description, and attachments.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to submit a support request while signed in. The new ticket will be connected to your account and available under My Tickets.

Fields and Options

Category
Choose the area that best matches the issue.
Subject
Enter a short, specific description of the request.
Description
Explain the issue, expected result, and relevant details.
Attachments
Add screenshots or supporting files when useful.

How to Use This Page

  1. Choose a category.
  2. Enter a clear subject.
  3. Describe the request in enough detail for support to begin investigating.
  4. Attach supporting files when needed.
  5. Submit the ticket.

What Happens Next

The ticket appears in My Tickets, where you can review responses and add follow-up information.

entries.title: Managing My Tickets
entries.summary: Review the status and history of support requests connected to your account.
entries.content:
About This Page

My Tickets lists support requests associated with your signed-in account.

Page Features

Ticket list
Review ticket number, subject, category, priority, status, and recent activity.
Create ticket
Start a new support request.
Ticket workspace
Open a ticket to read replies, add information, close it, or reopen it when allowed.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review open and recently updated tickets.
  2. Open the ticket related to your issue.
  3. Create a new request only when the matter is separate from an existing ticket.

entries.title: Using a Support Ticket
entries.summary: Review the conversation, reply to support, and close or reopen the ticket when allowed.
entries.content:
About This Page

The support ticket page shows the complete conversation and the current status of one request.

Page Features

Conversation
Read messages from you and the support team in chronological order.
Add a reply
Send additional information or answer a support question.
Close ticket
Mark a resolved ticket as closed when the action is available.
Reopen ticket
Return a closed ticket to the support queue when more help is required and reopening is allowed.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the newest messages and current ticket status.
  2. Enter a reply when support needs more information or the issue continues.
  3. Select Send reply.
  4. Close the ticket after the issue is resolved.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Keep replies focused on the same issue. Create a new ticket for an unrelated request.

entries.title: My Account Overview
entries.summary: Review purchases, licenses, saved assets, notifications, and personalized activity.
entries.content:
About This Page

My Account is the starting point for managing your Unclad Collection activity. It summarizes your library, licenses, wish lists, downloads, recent activity, and items that need attention.

Page Features

Licensed assets
Shows how many assets are available in your library.
Active licenses
Shows licenses that are currently active.
Saved assets
Opens your wish lists and saved items.
Downloads used
Summarizes download activity.
Needs your attention
Highlights account items that may require action.
Recent purchases and recommendations
Provides quick access to recently purchased, viewed, and recommended assets.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review any alerts under Needs your attention.
  2. Open a summary card to view the related account area.
  3. Use recent purchases, recently viewed items, or recommendations to continue your work.

entries.title: Browsing the Asset Library
entries.summary: Search, filter, and compare available media in the Digital Asset Library.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Digital Asset Library is the main marketplace browsing page. Use it to find assets by keyword, category, collection, tag, type, format, dimensions, orientation, or AI status.

Page Features

Search
Enter words that describe the subject, activity, setting, style, or purpose you need.
Filters
Narrow results by category, collection, tag, asset type, file format, orientation, minimum dimensions, or AI-generated status.
Active filters
Review and remove individual filter chips without clearing the entire search.
Result cards
Open an asset to review previews, files, pricing, and license options.

How to Use This Page

  1. Enter a search term or begin with the full library.
  2. Apply only the filters that are important to your project.
  3. Review the active filter chips and remove filters that are too restrictive.
  4. Open a result to review the asset details and available packages.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Start with a broad search, then add filters gradually.
  • Minimum width and height filters are measured in pixels.

entries.title: Understanding an Asset
entries.summary: Review previews, technical details, licensing packages, and related assets.
entries.content:
About This Page

The asset details page contains the information needed to decide whether an asset fits your project and which package or license to purchase.

Page Features

Preview gallery
Review the available presentation images or media previews.
Asset information
Read the title, description, creator information, classifications, and other descriptive details.
Choose the right package
Compare available offerings, file combinations, quantities, and license pricing.
Files and technical details
Review formats, dimensions, and included files before purchasing.
Related and recently viewed assets
Continue browsing similar or previously viewed content.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the preview and description.
  2. Confirm that the technical details meet your requirements.
  3. Choose an available package and license option.
  4. Complete any required quantity or shipping information.
  5. Add the selection to your cart or save the asset to a wish list.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Confirm the license and included files before checkout.
  • A shipping address may be required for physical or shipped offerings.

entries.title: Browsing Stories
entries.summary: Find articles and community content by search, category, or tag.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Stories page provides access to articles, education, news, and community-focused content published by Unclad Collection.

Page Features

Search
Find stories containing a topic or phrase.
Categories and tags
Narrow the list to a subject area.
Story cards
Open an article to read the full content and related information.

How to Use This Page

  1. Browse the newest stories or enter a search term.
  2. Apply a category or tag when you want a narrower topic.
  3. Open a story to read the complete article.

entries.title: Reading and Using a Story
entries.summary: Read an article, explore related media, and participate where comments are available.
entries.content:
About This Page

A Story page presents the full article together with author details, categories, related marketplace assets, and supported community features.

Page Features

Article content
Contains the complete published story.
Author and publication details
Identifies the contributor and publication information.
Related assets
Links to marketplace media connected with the story.
Comments
Allows eligible users to read or participate in the discussion when enabled.

How to Use This Page

  1. Read the story and review any related media.
  2. Open a related asset when you want licensing details.
  3. Use comments responsibly when participation is enabled.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Comments and marketplace licenses are governed separately from the article itself.

entries.title: Browsing a Collection
entries.summary: Explore a curated group of related assets.
entries.content:
About This Page

A Collection groups marketplace assets around a theme, subject, campaign, season, or editorial purpose.

Page Features

Collection description
Explains the purpose and focus of the collection.
Asset results
Displays the assets currently included in the collection.
Asset details
Opens licensing, technical information, and purchase options for an asset.

How to Use This Page

  1. Read the collection description.
  2. Browse the included assets.
  3. Open an asset to review its details and licensing options.

entries.title: Unsubscribe Confirmed
entries.summary: Your communication preference change has been recorded.
entries.content:
About This Page

This confirmation means the unsubscribe request was accepted for the communication category shown.

What Happens Next

Future optional messages in the affected category should no longer be sent to the associated recipient. Messages already queued before the change may still arrive.

Manage Other Preferences

Signed-in members can use their account communication settings to review or change additional notification and email preferences.

Important Notes

  • Essential transactional, security, purchase, licensing, or legally required messages may still be sent.
  • Keep your account email address current so important service messages reach you.

entries.title: Communication Preferences
entries.summary: Confirm whether you want to stop receiving a category of optional email communication.
entries.content:
About This Page

This page is opened from a secure email link and allows you to unsubscribe from the displayed category of optional communication.

Information on This Page

Communication Category

Identifies the type of email affected by this request.

Email Address or Account

Shows the recipient associated with the secure unsubscribe link when the page displays it.

Confirm Unsubscribe

Applies the preference change for the displayed communication category.

How to Unsubscribe

  1. Confirm that the displayed communication category is the one you want to stop receiving.
  2. Select the unsubscribe confirmation action.
  3. Wait for the confirmation page before closing the browser window.

Tips and Important Notes

  • This change normally affects optional communication in the displayed category, not essential account, purchase, security, or legal messages.
  • Signed-in members can review broader communication preferences from their account settings.
  • Do not forward secure preference links to other people.

entries.title: Using the Unclad Collection Home Page
entries.summary: Explore featured assets, collections, stories, and key areas of the marketplace.
entries.content:
About This Page

The home page introduces Unclad Collection and provides direct access to featured media, curated collections, community stories, and marketplace actions.

Page Features

Featured content
Open highlighted assets, collections, or stories selected for the home page.
Search and navigation
Use the site navigation and search tools to move directly to the content you need.
Calls to action
Use the available buttons to browse media, learn about licensing, or explore community content.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the featured sections to understand what is currently highlighted.
  2. Select an asset or collection to view its details.
  3. Use the main navigation or search when you already know what you need.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Home-page content may change as collections, seasonal content, and featured assets are updated.

entries.title: Image Details
entries.summary: Review an image preview, description, categories, tags, availability, and purchasing options.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this page to review a marketplace image before adding it to a wish list, cart, or purchase workflow.

Page Information

Preview

Shows the marketplace preview. Preview files may be resized or watermarked and are not the licensed deliverable.

Title and Description

Explain the image subject, setting, activity, and intended context.

Categories and Tags

Help describe and organize the image and can be used to discover related content.

License and Price Options

Show the available purchasing terms and prices when the image can be licensed.

Favorites or Wish List

Saves the image for later review when you are signed in.

Related Images

Suggest other content that may fit a similar subject or use.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the preview and description carefully.
  2. Confirm that the subject and available file meet your intended use.
  3. Review the license option before adding the image to the cart.
  4. Save the image to a wish list when you are not ready to purchase.
  5. Continue to checkout when the selected image and license are correct.

Tips and Important Notes

  • A preview is not a licensed production file.
  • Purchase the license that matches how the image will be used.
  • Review restrictions and model or property information displayed with the asset.

entries.title: Information Page
entries.summary: Read the published information, policies, frequently asked questions, or contact content provided on this page.
entries.content:
About This Page

This is a published Unclad Collection information page. Its specific purpose depends on the page title and may include company information, policies, frequently asked questions, or contact guidance.

Using This Page

  1. Review the page heading and introductory content.
  2. Use section links or frequently asked questions when they are available.
  3. Follow any displayed call-to-action or contact instructions that apply to your question.
  4. Use the Support Center when the page does not resolve an account, order, license, or technical issue.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Policy and license pages should be reviewed before purchasing or using marketplace content.
  • Contact forms should not include passwords or complete payment-card information.
  • The content shown is the currently published version maintained by site administrators.

entries.title: Viewing a Shared Wish List
entries.summary: Browse assets another member has chosen to share.
entries.content:
About This Page

A Shared Wish List provides read-only access to an unlisted list through its share link.

Page Features

List information
Shows the list name and any description supplied by its owner.
Shared assets
Opens available assets in the marketplace.
Availability notice
Identifies when an asset is no longer available to public viewers.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the purpose of the list.
  2. Open an available asset to view current details and licensing.
  3. Contact the list owner outside the site when you need changes to the list.

Tips and Important Notes

  • The shared page does not give visitors permission to edit the owner’s list.

entries.title: Submitting a Support Request
entries.summary: Send a new support request with contact details, a description, and optional attachments.
entries.content:
About This Page

Use this form to contact the support team when you need help with the site, an order, licensing, downloads, billing, or another issue.

Fields and Options

Name
Enter the name support should use when replying.
Email
Enter a valid email address where you can receive responses.
Category
Choose the category that best describes the request.
Subject
Enter a brief summary of the issue.
What can we help with?
Describe what happened, what you expected, and any steps already attempted.
Attachments
Add relevant screenshots or files when they will help explain the issue.

How to Use This Page

  1. Enter your name and email address.
  2. Choose the closest category.
  3. Write a clear subject and detailed description.
  4. Add useful attachments when available.
  5. Select Submit request.

What Happens Next

The system creates a support ticket and provides confirmation. Keep the ticket information so you can follow future responses.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Do not include passwords or full payment-card information.
  • Include order numbers, license keys, or exact error messages when relevant.

entries.title: Guest Support Ticket
entries.summary: Review a support request submitted without an account and continue the conversation securely.
entries.content:
About This Page

This page displays a guest support ticket using its secure access link. It shows the request, replies, attachments, and current status.

Ticket Information

Ticket Number

The reference number used when communicating with support.

Status

Shows whether the ticket is open, waiting, resolved, closed, or in another supported state.

Conversation

Displays the original request and all visible replies in chronological order.

Attachments

Provides access to files associated with the ticket when they are available to guests.

Reply

Allows you to add information or answer a support question while the ticket accepts replies.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the latest message and current ticket status.
  2. Download or review attachments that are relevant to the conversation.
  3. Enter a concise reply when support needs more information.
  4. Attach only files that help explain the issue.
  5. Submit the reply and return using the same secure link for future updates.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Treat the guest ticket link as private because it provides access to the conversation.
  • Do not post passwords, complete payment-card numbers, or highly sensitive personal information.
  • If the ticket is closed and the issue returns, follow the available reopen instructions or create a new request.

entries.title: Using the Support Center
entries.summary: Review support information, frequently asked questions, or begin a request.
entries.content:
About This Page

The public Support page explains how to get help and provides answers to common questions before a ticket is submitted.

Page Features

Support FAQ
Review common questions and answers.
Submit a request
Open the support form when the FAQ does not resolve the issue.
Member support
Signed-in members can review existing tickets from their account.

How to Use This Page

  1. Review the FAQ for a quick answer.
  2. Select the option to submit a support request when more help is needed.
  3. Sign in before submitting when you want the request connected to your account.

entries.title: Support Center
entries.summary: Choose the appropriate way to request help or review an existing support conversation.
entries.content:
About This Page

The Support Center helps visitors and members find the correct path for requesting assistance.

Available Options

Submit a Request

Starts a new support request when you need help with the website, an account, a purchase, licensing, advertising, or another supported topic.

Member Tickets

Signed-in members can review and continue their existing support tickets.

Guest Ticket Access

Guests can return to a submitted ticket using the secure link provided after submission or by email.

How to Get Help

  1. Choose the option that matches whether you are signed in and whether a ticket already exists.
  2. Provide a clear description of the issue or question.
  3. Include relevant order, asset, campaign, or error information without sharing passwords or complete payment-card details.
  4. Keep the confirmation or secure ticket link so you can review replies.

Tips and Important Notes

  • Create one ticket per issue whenever possible.
  • Reply to the existing ticket instead of opening duplicates.
  • Urgent safety or emergency matters should be directed to the appropriate emergency service rather than website support.
